boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, named academic environments at Muhlenberg, selected for documented research, writing, computing, collections, or academic-space features.

cards.title: Trexler Library
cards.subtitle: Three-floor library on the south side of Chew Street
cards.notes: Start with the library’s three floors, then choose a workspace style that fits your task: carrels, couches, bean bag chairs, or collaborative areas.
cards.short_summary: A campus research and study hub with several workspace formats.
cards.evidence_claim: Trexler Library describes spaces for noisy collaborative work and silent independent study, with workspaces ranging from carrels to couches and bean bag chairs.
cards.access_notes: Hours may change; a Muhlenberg ID is required to enter after 8 p.m., and doors lock 15 minutes before closing.

cards.title: AT&T Information Commons
cards.subtitle: Trexler Library
cards.notes: Use this named library destination when your work needs a computer-oriented setting; confirm open equipment and building access before settling in.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed information commons inside Trexler Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Muhlenberg’s current printable campus map lists the AT&T Information Commons within Trexler Library.
cards.access_notes: Located in Trexler Library; follow current library access guidance and hours.

cards.title: Altman Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Fahy Commons
cards.notes: Head to this named reading room in Fahy Commons for a defined academic stop, and check the building’s posted access conditions on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed reading room in the college’s public-engagement and innovation building.
cards.evidence_claim: Muhlenberg’s current printable campus map lists the Altman Reading Room in Fahy Commons.
cards.access_notes: Located in Fahy Commons; consult building signage for current access.

cards.title: Rare Books Exhibit Room
cards.subtitle: B-Level, Trexler Library
cards.notes: Check whether the room is reserved; when it is open, combine a study session with time viewing the rotating special-collections exhibit.
cards.short_summary: An exhibit room that doubles as open student study space when unreserved.
cards.evidence_claim: The library states that when not reserved, the Rare Books Exhibit Room is open for students to study or for patrons to view its rotating exhibits.
cards.access_notes: On B-Level. Faculty and staff may reserve it; availability for study depends on the reservation schedule.

cards.title: Muhlenberg Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Main level, Trexler Library
cards.notes: Bring a draft or assignment question and use the center as a focused writing-work stop; review the center’s current appointment guidance first.
cards.short_summary: A library-based academic support space for writing work.
cards.evidence_claim: Muhlenberg states that its Writing Center is located on the main level of Trexler Library and supports students across disciplines.
cards.access_notes: Located on Trexler Library’s main level; check the Writing Center page for current service details.

cards.title: Special Collections and College Archives
cards.subtitle: Level B, Trexler Library
cards.notes: Plan a primary-source research session by contacting the archives ahead of time, so requested materials can be prepared for your arrival.
cards.short_summary: An appointment-based primary-source research setting in the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Trexler Library identifies Special Collections and College Archives on Level B and says materials may be viewed by appointment Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Make an appointment in advance; materials are non-circulating and certain items may have access restrictions.

cards.title: Trexler Library Reading Terraces
cards.subtitle: Trexler Library interior
cards.notes: Choose the reading terraces when you want a defined library seating area; pair them with materials from the nearby collections or your own work.
cards.short_summary: Named interior reading terraces in Trexler Library.
cards.evidence_claim: A Muhlenberg College magazine feature identifies Trexler Library’s open staircase as bordering its reading terraces.
cards.source_title: 25th Anniversary of Trexler Library: An Ever Adapting Space
cards.access_notes: Inside Trexler Library; follow current library hours and access guidance.

cards.title: Trexler Library Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Trexler Library
cards.notes: Use a study carrel for an independent work block, then shift to another library area if your task needs conversation or shared screens.
cards.short_summary: Individual library workstations among Trexler’s documented workspace options.
cards.evidence_claim: Trexler Library lists study carrels among the workspace types it provides for different study needs.
cards.access_notes: Inside Trexler Library; availability is first-come and subject to current building access.

cards.entity_name: Fahy Commons for Public Engagement and Innovation
cards.title: Fahy Commons for Public Engagement and Innovation
cards.subtitle: Academic and programming space on campus
cards.notes: Set up here when your work benefits from an academic building that also houses the Makerspace, community engagement, and innovation programs.
cards.short_summary: A 20,000-square-foot academic and programming building with multiple campus programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Muhlenberg describes Fahy Commons as providing 20,000 square feet of programming, art studio, and academic space and housing the Makerspace.
cards.access_notes: Check current building access and any program-specific requirements before using spaces.

cards.title: Baker Center for the Arts
cards.subtitle: Academic arts building
cards.notes: Use the building as a change-of-scene academic stop when your coursework connects to art, writing, music, theatre, or dance spaces.
cards.short_summary: An arts academic building with studios, shops, classrooms, and performance spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Muhlenberg states that the Baker Center for the Arts contains studios, shops, classrooms, and performance spaces and houses art, English, music, theatre, and dance.
cards.access_notes: Building spaces may be scheduled for classes, rehearsals, or events; observe posted access directions.
